subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during an ongoing dungeon delve, following prior encounters with Derro and culminating in the discovery of a ritual chamber. The timeline is continuous, with no temporal breaks.
source_quote: Our journey continues until we reach another cave entrance.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during the current session of the campaign, as implied by the immediate, in-character narration and lack of temporal markers beyond 'now' and 'just now.'
source_quote: I look at him carefully. He has blue, gray skin and pale eyes that lack both irises and pupils.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during the ongoing journey through the subterranean labyrinth of Gracklstugh, following the collapse of prior alliances and the emergence of the Ember Vanguard as a new, unstable force.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the Derro has blue, gray skin and pale eyes that lack both irises and pupils.
source_quote: He has blue, gray skin and pale eyes that lack both irises and pupils.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the Derro has thin, stringy hair, dull white, constantly looking greasy and unkempt.
source_quote: He has thin, stringy hair, dull white, constantly looking greasy and unkempt.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the Derro is muttering to himself.
source_quote: Now that’s interesting, he seems to be muttering to himself.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the Derro is wearing scraps of tattered leather and cloth stained with grime and foul odors.
source_quote: The creature is wearing scraps of tattered leather and cloth stained with grime and the foul odors of wherever he has been working.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the books made from Trillimac on the platform.
source_quote: Around the platform are books made from Trillimac.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform.
source_quote: The cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform.
source_quote: A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the titles of the books: “The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,” “The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn,” and “Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.”
source_quote: I look carefully and notice a few of the titles - “The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,” and “The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn”, and “Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized Ulnara’s arrogance disappeared and her subservient persona emerged.
source_quote: Her arrogance disappears, and her sniveling, subservient persona emerges.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recalled the stories of the Derro, creatures that served the mind flayers and had their minds destroyed.
source_quote: I recall the stories of the Derro, creatures that served the mind flayers and had their minds destroyed.

subject: Daz kills Skiit with Toll the Dead
fact: Daz casts Toll the Dead, a spell only audible to its target, causing Skiit’s heart to stop and killing him instantly.
source_quote: I cast Toll the Dead, and the deadly chimes echo throughout the caves, but only it’s intended target hears them, and his heart stops, and he dies.

subject: Daz orders companions to wait outside the brimstone cavern
fact: Daz instructs Jim Jar, Spiderbait, Sarith, Eldeth, and Stool to remain outside the cavern filled with brimstone and chemicals while he enters alone.
source_quote: We tell our companions to wait outside. Jim Jar, Spiderbait, Sarith, Eldeth, and Stool look at me worried, but I motion for them to stay.

subject: daz's spellcasting
fact: Daz casts Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp, Toll the Dead, and Magic Missile against Derro.
source_quote: I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp... I cast Toll the Dead... launched his magic missiles

subject: derro madness
fact: Derro are described as former slaves of mind flayers, corrupted until barely dwarves, and irredeemably insane.
source_quote: The Derro themselves were predictably clumsy... Dwarves that were slaves of the mindflayers, who corrupted their fundamental nature until they are barely Dwarves. They are mad.

subject: Derro Patrol Attack
fact: A Derro patrol attacks the party after Grygum declares his worship of Bahamut, triggering violent chaos; Thorin kills two Derro with his sword, Daz uses magic missiles, and Zalthir summons darkness, demonstrating the Derro’s inability to reason and their fatal devotion to Demogorgon.

subject: Derro patrol attacks after hearing 'Bahamut'
fact: A Derro patrol immediately attacks the party after Grygum declares 'I worship Bahamut,' revealing their intolerance for any deity outside Demogorgon.
source_quote: The moment that Grygum mentioned 'Bahamut,' I knew we were in for it. ... they immediately attack.

subject: Derro Patrol Encounter
fact: A Derro patrol stumbles upon the party, but Daz's show of dominance causes them to retreat in fear, demonstrating that the Derro are more terrified of perceived authority than they are aggressive when unprovoked.
source_quote: Daz insists we march as if we own this place. And it works. The creatures are fearful and somewhat deranged.

subject: Discovery of Demogorgon Evidence
fact: The party uncovers concrete, physical evidence linking the Derro to Demogorgon’s influence through ritual texts and papers. This discovery creates moral tension, as Daz considers withholding it from Errde Blackstaff to prevent ideological manipulation.
source_quote: Errde Blackstaff wants evidence of Demogorgon’s influence, and here it is.

subject: experiment session
fact: An experiment session is underway, led by Narrak, involving apprentices chanting in response to his declarations of purpose.
source_quote: He shouts - 'We are conducting experiments!'... They chant back at him - 'For what purpose!'

subject: Great Project of Ulnara
fact: A massive necromantic endeavor under the Council of Savants, involving the reanimation of corpses and the collection of body parts for unknown purposes. It is overseen by Ulnara and staffed by Derro laborers like Skiit, who fear failure and crave Pliinki’s approval.
source_quote: ‘The great project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants!’

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum pushed Skiit over the cliff.
source_quote: I push him over the cliff.

subject: Grygum claims the name 'Ember Vanguard'
fact: Grygum declares the group as the 'Ember Vanguard,' a name Daz approves of and which is later used to intimidate Derro and other inhabitants.
source_quote: 'We are the Ember Guard,' shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: Grygum pushes Skiit into the pit
fact: Grygum pushes Skiit over the cliff while Daz unleashes a light show, initiating the confrontation with Ulnara.
source_quote: I push him over the cliff. At the same time, Daz unleashes a light show.

subject: Grygum's Bahamut Declaration
fact: Grygum’s religious proclamation triggers immediate violent hostility from the Derro, who perceive Bahamut as a heretical blasphemy against their two-headed deity. This event forces the party into combat despite prior non-confrontational intentions.
source_quote: The moment that Grygum mentioned 'Bahamut,' I knew we were in for it.

subject: grygum's combat actions
fact: Grygum is struck by Derro, defended by allies, and survives combat with divine protection.
source_quote: The other landed a hit on Grygum... our allies were quick to retaliate

subject: grygum's divine scrutiny
fact: Grygum frames the question 'Who do you work for?' as a Divine Scrutiny, invoking Celestial Archives and Divine Ledgers.
source_quote: It is, in fact, a Divine Scrutiny, a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates... Divine Ledgers or Celestial Archives

subject: Grygum’s Divine Scrutiny
fact: Grygum performs a Divine Scrutiny on Ulnara, framing the question 'Who do you work for?' as a profound theological inquiry, using elaborate rhetoric to confuse and manipulate her, revealing the group’s internal disunity and performative piety.

subject: grygum's worship declaration
fact: Grygum declares worship of Bahamut, triggering immediate Derro hostility.
source_quote: I worship Bahamut!

subject: Narrak leads Derro ritual
fact: Narrak leads a Derro ritual involving chanting apprentices and the reading of forbidden texts to achieve the triumph of Demogorgon and the destruction of the Duergar.
source_quote: He shouts - 'We are conducting experiments!' ... 'The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!'

subject: narrak's experiment
fact: Narrak conducts experiments to elevate the Derro, triumph Demogorgon, and destroy the Duergar.
source_quote: We are conducting experiments!... The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: Skiit’s Death
fact: Skiit is thrown into a pit by Grygum, then targeted by Daz’s magic; he briefly revives, escapes Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp, but is ultimately killed by Toll the Dead, his final words revealing his delusional belief in Demogorgon’s favor.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed two Derro in front of a tent, both talking while ignoring each other.
source_quote: I notice two Derro in front of a tent, near a tent. Both are talking while ignoring each other.

subject: Thorin declares 'East' as a direction
fact: Thorin, exhausted by debate, arbitrarily chooses 'East' as the path forward, ending a discussion among the group.
source_quote: Left or right?' I ask. ... 'East.'

subject: Thorin dismisses two mad Derro as worthless
fact: Thorin observes two Derro babbling incoherently near a tent and declares there is nothing of value there, leading the group to move on without conflict.
source_quote: No. There is nothing of value here.

subject: thorin's eastward decision
fact: Thorin chooses 'East' as the path forward, ending a debate and guiding the party's direction.
source_quote: I say - 'East.'

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: Ulnara transforms from arrogance to subservience
fact: Ulnara’s demeanor shifts from arrogance to fearful subservience upon realizing Daz is a Drow, demonstrating the terror Drow inspire among Derro.
source_quote: She realizes that I am Drow. And that the Drow do not mess around. ... Her arrogance disappears, and her sniveling, subservient persona emerges.

subject: zalthir's silent observation
fact: Zalthir observes all without speaking, acting with clarity and purpose.
source_quote: I observe everything and say nothing. My mind is clear. I act without speaking. I do because I know.

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: A pervasive and dangerous cult among the Derro, led by figures like Pliinki, that promises power and renewal to those who follow Demogorgon. Skiit and Ulnara are adherents, using devotion to the Prince of Demons to justify their actions and maintain morale despite their broken minds.
source_quote: ‘I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful.’

subject: Cult of Demogorgon
fact: The Cult of Demogorgon is actively entrenched among the Derro, who believe their madness and atrocities are divine acts of elevation; they revere the Two-Headed Beast, perform rituals using forbidden texts, and view the Duergar as enemies to be destroyed.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are a race of twisted, insane dwarven offshoots once enslaved by mind flayers, now serving as laborers and cultists in the Underdark. They are mentally broken, prone to muttering, and often worship Demogorgon as a source of false hope. They are not well in the best of times.
source_quote: I recall the stories of the Derro, creatures that served the mind flayers and had their minds destroyed. They are not well in the best of times.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are being elevated as part of a ritualistic agenda tied to Demogorgon's triumph and the destruction of the Duergar.
source_quote: He screams - 'The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!'

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are former slaves of the mind flayers whose minds were destroyed, now serving Demogorgon and driven to madness and ritualistic devotion.
source_quote: The Derro are Dwarves that were slaves of the mindflayers, who corrupted their fundamental nature until they are barely Dwarves. They are mad.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are mind-flayer-corrupted dwarves, driven insane and devoted to Demogorgon, who serve as laborers, necromancers, and ritualists in underground complexes, muttering incoherently, obsessed with body parts, and incapable of rational discourse.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are referenced by Derro as enemies to be destroyed, and by Skiit as a possible master group that the Ember Vanguard might serve.
source_quote: I think you work for the Duergar or the Mindflayers!

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are targeted for destruction as part of the Derro's ritualistic agenda under Demogorgon's influence.
source_quote: He screams - 'The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!'

subject: Ember Guard
fact: The Ember Guard is a self-proclaimed faction led by Grygum and Daz, presented as a powerful, mysterious group to intimidate Derro and other denizens of Gracklstugh. The name was chosen by Grygum to project authority, though its true nature and allegiance are ambiguous and possibly fabricated.
source_quote: ‘We are the Ember Guard,’ shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a group led by Grygum and Daz that claims authority over the Derro-infested caves, using the name to intimidate and command respect.
source_quote: We are the Ember Guard," shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a mysterious group that presents itself as a unified force, though its members are fractured in allegiance and purpose; Grygum claims it as a divine entity, Daz operates under its banner, and it is mistaken by Derro for either Duergar or Mindflayer agents.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a specialized unit trained for stealth and infiltration in hostile, hazardous environments. They operate independently from their companions, using darkness and silence to navigate dangerous terrain, and prioritize mission objectives over safety or consensus.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard will march in, but we tell our companions to wait outside.

subject: cage chamber
fact: A chamber lined with scrap iron cages on both sides contains a spiral path marked by small stone pylons, emitting a foul odor.
source_quote: The smell is coming from cages assembled from scrap iron on both sides of the chamber. A spiral path circles into the center of the room, marked off by small stone pylons.

subject: cage chamber
fact: Cages assembled from scrap iron line the chamber, with Derro speaking of the prince's hunger.
source_quote: cages assembled from scrap iron on both sides of the chamber

subject: cave entrance with brimstone smell
fact: The cave entrance reeks of brimstone and chemicals, signaling a demonic presence.
source_quote: the unspeakable stench... smell of brimstone and chemicals

subject: Derro Cage Chamber
fact: The Derro Cage Chamber is a dark room lined with scrap-iron cages, a spiral path marked by stone pylons, and two deranged Derro who speak in riddles about the 'prince's hunger' and 'dark lake scales,' emitting a foul odor that nearly overwhelms the party.

subject: Derro Chamber with Scrap Iron Cages
fact: This chamber is filled with scrap iron cages, spiral stone pylons marking a central path, and bubbling cauldrons emitting a foul, nauseating stench. It is a site of ritualistic madness, where Derro conduct forbidden experiments and worship their twisted deities.
source_quote: The smell is coming from cages assembled from scrap iron on both sides of the chamber. A spiral path circles into the center of the room, marked off by small stone pylons.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: A sprawling, chaotic Underdark city where the Ember Guard operates. It is a place of fractured loyalties, necromantic projects, and deranged Derro laborers. The city’s environment is thick with faerzress and the stench of death.
source_quote: a profound act of investigation into the very threads of our intertwined fates, here in this churning city of Gracklstugh.

subject: Pit of Ulnara
fact: The Pit of Ulnara is a massive, stinking chasm filled with decomposing body parts and shambling zombies, used for harvesting flesh and creating undead, with a narrow tunnel leading from its southeast wall and glowing faerzress fog swirling around it.

subject: pit of Ulnara
fact: The pit is filled with body parts and reeks of death and decomposed flesh.
source_quote: tossing body parts over the ledge into the pit

subject: pit trap
fact: A poorly disguised pit trap is hidden in the cavern entrance, indicating the presence of defensive measures by the Derro inhabitants.
source_quote: Watch it! ... a poorly disguised pit trap.

subject: ritual cavern
fact: A glowing ritual circle dominates a 5-foot-high platform, surrounded by books on Demogorgon and Derro madness.
source_quote: a glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform... books made from Trillimac

subject: Ritual Cavern of Narrak
fact: The Ritual Cavern of Narrak is a hellish chamber with red spiral walls, glowing ritual circles, and books on Demogorgon’s influence; it is inhabited by Derro and death dogs, and contains forbidden tomes like 'The Spiraling Descent' and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Ritual Cavern of the Two-Headed Beast
fact: This cavern glows with hellish red light, features spiral wall patterns, silent dripping water, and rampant fungi. At its center is a ritual circle atop a 5-foot platform, surrounded by forbidden tomes on duality, madness, and spawn creation, indicating deep Demogorgon influence and Derro heresy.
source_quote: The cavern floor rises to form a natural 5-foot-high platform. A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform. Around the platform are books made from Trillimac...

subject: ritual platform
fact: A glowing ritual circle dominates a 5-foot-high platform in a cavern, surrounded by Trillimac books titled 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn,' and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'
source_quote: A glowing ritual circle dominates the top of the platform. Around the platform are books made from Trillimac. I look carefully and notice a few of the titles - 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' and 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn', and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: The Pit
fact: A massive, foul-smelling chasm in the tunnel system of Gracklstugh, filled with decomposing flesh, offal, fungi, and shambling zombies. It serves as the disposal and reanimation site for the Great Project of Ulnara, with a narrow tunnel leading from its southeast wall.
source_quote: The glow of faerzress is everywhere, seeming to flow like fog around dark shapes shambling across the pit. A crack in the southeast wall of the pit leads to a narrow tunnel, flanked by mounds of fungi and offal.

subject: ulnara's laboratory
fact: Ulnara, a Derro necromancer and Demogorgon cultist, oversees the creation of undead from pit offerings.
source_quote: Ulnara... necromancer in charge... cultist of Demogorgon... turn him into a zombie

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Death Dogs
fact: Death Dogs are spectral, bestial predators associated with the Derro and their ritual sites. They are silent, lurking, and attuned to the cursed energies of the caverns, serving as guardians or hunting companions to the mad dwarves.
source_quote: I finally spot the inhabitants, some Derro and Death dogs.

subject: death dogs
fact: Death dogs are present alongside Derro in the ritual cavern.
source_quote: some Derro and Death dogs

subject: Death dogs
fact: Death dogs are present in the cavern with the ritual platform, sharing space with Derro and unaware of the Ember Vanguard’s approach.
source_quote: And I finally spot the inhabitants, some Derro and Death dogs.

subject: Demogorgon
fact: Demogorgon is the demon lord being served by Narrak, whose influence drives the Derro's campaign of elevation and destruction.
source_quote: He screams - 'The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!'

subject: derro count
fact: A single Derro stands over a pit with an unbelievable smell emanating from it.
source_quote: a single Derro standing over a pit, with an unbelievable smell emanating from it

subject: derro patrol
fact: A Derro patrol stumbles upon the party, displaying fear and derangement.
source_quote: a Derro patrol stumbles on us

subject: narrak
fact: Narrak, a Derro with warped intellect, leads experiments in service to Demogorgon.
source_quote: This is Narrak... his eyes dart about with a frenetic, almost desperate energy... warped intellect simmering beneath his frantic movements

subject: Ogre Zombie
fact: An Ogre Zombie emerges from a crack in the southeast wall of the pit, demanding to know who the intruders are.
source_quote: From there, a voice and an Ogre Zombie emerge. 'What is the meaning of this? Who are you? Who do you think you are?'

subject: Ogre Zombie
fact: An undead Ogre Zombie emerged from the pit, demanding to know the identity of the intruders. It is one of many reanimated corpses serving Ulnara’s necromantic project, and its presence confirms the scale of the Great Project’s corpse consumption.
source_quote: From there, a voice and an Ogre Zombie emerge. ‘What is the meaning of this? Who are you? Who do you think you are?’

subject: skiit
fact: Skiit, a Derro cultist of Demogorgon, is thrown into the pit and later resurrected as a zombie.
source_quote: Skiit looks at me and then points at Spiderbait... I push him over the cliff... turn him into a zombie

subject: Zombies
fact: Numerous zombies populate the pit beneath the Derro’s work site, reanimated corpses used as laborers or components in Ulnara’s necromantic project. Grygum observes them and uses their presence to manipulate Skiit’s fear and ambition.
source_quote: ‘I see a lot of zombies.’

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes the Derro is a dummy that needs someone else to think for him and is therefore a true believer.
source_quote: I wonder is he the true-believing kind that has warped his world view? Or is he just a dummy that needs someone else to think for him and is therefore a true believer?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Drow spellcaster who employs lethal magic with clinical precision, kills Derro with spells like Toll the Dead and Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp, and recognizes the cultist Ulnara as a Demogorgon devotee while exploiting her fear of Drow authority.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Drow spellcaster who employs lethal magic with precision and psychological dominance. He cast Maximilian’s Earthen Grasp and Toll the Dead to kill Skiit, and uses fear to subdue enemies. He recognizes Ulnara as a Derro necromancer and cultist of Demogorgon, and exploits her superstition by revealing his Drow identity to crush her arrogance.
source_quote: I look at Ulnara, who realizes that I am Drow. And that the Drow do not mess around.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Drow who casts Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp, Toll the Dead, and magic missiles, kills Skiit, and intimidates Ulnara by revealing his Drow identity.
source_quote: I cast Maximillian’s Earthen Grasp and start to crush the poor unfortunate creature. I cast Toll the Dead, and the deadly chimes echo throughout the caves, but only it’s intended target hears them, and his heart stops, and he dies.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a battle-hardened dwarf warrior clad in heavy armor, known for his blunt combat style and dark humor. He relies on brute force and intimidation, and his actions in battle are decisive, if unrefined.
source_quote: I swung my longsword, a satisfying *thwack* as it connected. 'Take that, you blithering fool!' I yelled.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is leading the party through the caves, asserting dominance over Derro and making tactical decisions despite fatigue. He is skeptical of authority figures like Errde Blackstaff and prioritizes practicality over ideological submission.
source_quote: I squint at the tents and the room and say, 'No. There is nothing of value here.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz knows he has struck numerous deals with various other parties and is no longer sure what to say when asked who he works for.
source_quote: We have struck numerous deals with various other parties, and I'm no longer sure what to say.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz knows that if he doesn’t give Errde Blackstaff evidence, she’ll invent it.
source_quote: I might not want to give it to her. But I know her type; if she doesn’t get evidence, she’ll invent it.

subject: Derro
fact: The Derro are corrupted, mad dwarves once enslaved by mindflayers, now worshiping a two-headed deity and obsessed with ritualistic madness. They are physically weak, intellectually limited, and violently reactive to deviations from their dogma, especially references to Bahamut.
source_quote: They are mad.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes Skiit is a follower of Demogorgon and is making the Derro proud and powerful.
source_quote: I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful. And we’re going to be great again!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the two Derro are mad.
source_quote: Grygum mutters, “They are mad.”

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum created the Divine magic chant for the believing, but it was theater he created for himself.
source_quote: That’s a bit of theater that I created for the believing. I should be honest, it’s theater I created for myself.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum finds Bahamut boring and Stroud exciting.
source_quote: Bahamut is boring. Stroud was exciting. Bahamut, not so much.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who uses theatrical divine incantations to inspire belief, though he finds Bahamut boring and was once inspired by Stroud. He is currently leading the Ember Guard through the tunnels of Gracklstugh, interrogating Derro and manipulating their fears. He pushed Skiit into the pit and later adopted the name 'Ember Guard' to project authority.
source_quote: ‘We are the Ember Guard,’ shouts Grygum. I smile. I like that name.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric of Bahamut who uses theatrical divine rhetoric to manipulate and interrogate Derro, often deflecting their madness with performative piety and psychological pressure, and has personally pushed a Derro named Skiit into a pit.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a worshipper of Bahamut who declares his faith aloud in the presence of Derro, provoking immediate hostility.
source_quote: I worship Bahamut!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a zealous preacher who reveres Bahamut and repeatedly interrupts tense situations with religious declarations, inadvertently provoking hostile Derro. His actions are driven by faith, not strategy, and he often fails to recognize the danger he creates.
source_quote: I worship Bahamut!

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak believes the purpose of their experiments is the elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar.
source_quote: The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a Derro orchestrator of forbidden rituals who shouts of experiments for the elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar.
source_quote: We are conducting experiments! For what purpose! The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a Derro ritual master and high priest of Demogorgon who conducts experiments in a hellish cavern, chants doctrines of Derro supremacy, and presides over forbidden texts like 'The Prince's Gift' and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Narrak
fact: Narrak is a derro orchestrator of a disturbing scene, perpetually contorted with spiraling madness, radiating chaotic evil in service to Demogorgon, and leading apprentices in forbidden experiments.
source_quote: He gestures wildly at a few apprentices... He shouts - 'We are conducting experiments!'... He screams - 'The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!'

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki is an unseen authority figure among the Derro, believed to be a leader or high priest who promises better jobs and divine favor to those who serve Demogorgon. Skiit and Ulnara both reference Pliinki’s words to justify their loyalty and actions.
source_quote: ‘But Pliinki promised Skiit a better job.’

subject: Skiit
fact: Skiit is a Derro cultist of Demogorgon who believes he serves a higher purpose, mutters obsessively about Pliinki and Skiit’s promised better job, and becomes a target of Grygum’s manipulation and Daz’s lethal magic after being thrown into a pit.

subject: Skiit
fact: Skiit is a Derro cultist of Demogorgon who mutters to himself and pleads for a better job after being promised one by Pliinki.
source_quote: But Pliinki promised Skiit a better job.

subject: Skiit
fact: Skiit is a Derro laborer working on the Great Project of Ulnara, obsessed with Pliinki’s promises and devoted to Demogorgon. He is mentally unstable, muttering to himself, and believes following Demogorgon makes the Derro proud. He was pushed into the pit by Grygum, resurrected as a corpse, and then killed by Daz’s Toll the Dead.
source_quote: ‘I am a follower of Demogorgon! Pliinki has said that anybody who follows Demogorgon is making the Derro proud and powerful.’

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the Derro are dwarves corrupted by mind flayers until they are barely dwarves.
source_quote: The Derro themselves were Dwarves that were slaves of the mindflayers, who corrupted their fundamental nature until they are barely Dwarves.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the Derro are not creatures to reason with.
source_quote: These are not creatures to reason with.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf warrior who relies on brute force and armor to dominate Derro in combat, kills multiple Derro with his longsword, dismisses their madness as unworthy of reasoning with, and makes impulsive decisions like declaring 'East' during navigation.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf who, exhausted by debate, arbitrarily chooses 'East' as a direction and dismisses two mad Derro as worthless.
source_quote: East.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is too tired to participate in the discussion about which way to go.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks the Derro don’t know how to take a bath.

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a Derro necromancer and Demogorgon cultist who oversees body-part harvesting for a 'great project,' transforms corpses into zombies, and shifts from arrogance to subservience upon realizing Daz is a Drow.

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a Derro necromancer and cultist of Demogorgon who oversees the great project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants and transforms into a subservient persona upon realizing Daz is a Drow.

subject: Ulnara
fact: Ulnara is a Derro necromancer and cultist of Demogorgon, in charge of the Great Project of Ulnara of the Council of Savants. She is subservient and fearful until confronted with Daz’s Drow identity, at which point she abandons her arrogance and becomes obsequious, offering zombie labor to the Ember Guard.
source_quote: ‘Thank you for this new supply! I know you will tell Pliinki that I Ulnara did much to help the Ember Vanguard!’

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a monk who observes silently, acts decisively without speech, and uses darkness magic to envelop Derro in combat, critically striking one with precise arcane speed while maintaining emotional detachment.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a monk who observes silently, acts without speaking, and summons darkness to envelop Derro during combat.
source_quote: I observe everything and say nothing. My mind is clear. I act without speaking. I do because I know.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an arcane specialist who uses precise, high-impact spells in combat. He excels at controlling the battlefield with darkness and delivering critical strikes, and his magic is instrumental in neutralizing Derro threats.
source_quote: Zalthir, bless his arcane heart, summoned his darkness, enveloping a couple of them. Then, in a burst of brilliant speed, he critically struck one of the Darrow.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observes everything and says nothing because his mind is clear and he acts because he knows.

subject: Zalthir

subject: Amulet of Demogorgon

subject: amulet of Demogorgon

subject: Amulet of Demogorgon
fact: The Amulet of Demogorgon is worn by Skiit and possibly others among the Derro; it is a visible symbol of their heretical devotion, and its presence confirms their transformation from laborers into fanatical cultists.

subject: demogorgon amulet value

subject: derro chant

source_quote: For what purpose!... The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!

subject: Dirty Finger Pattern Tracing

source_quote: tracing an invisible pattern with a dirty finger

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.

subject: Trillimac books
fact: Books bound in Trillimac contain treatises on Demogorgon’s influence, madness, and the creation of favored spawn, serving as evidence of the cult’s activities.
source_quote: Books made from Trillimac. I look carefully and notice a few of the titles - 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' and 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn', and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Trillimac Books
fact: The Trillimac Books are ancient, bound volumes found in Narrak’s ritual chamber, containing treatises on madness, duality, and Demogorgon’s favored spawn; they serve as irrefutable evidence of the demon lord’s influence on the Derro.

subject: Trillimac Books
fact: These books, bound in Trillimac, contain heretical texts on the Two-Headed Beast, duality, madness, and the creation of favored spawn. They are key evidence of Demogorgon’s influence and are sought by Errde Blackstaff for ideological validation.
source_quote: “The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,” and “The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn”, and “Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.”

subject: trillimac book titles
fact: Books include 'The Spiraling Descent: A Treatise on Duality and Madness,' 'The Prince's Gift: On the Creation of Favored Spawn,' and 'Rituals of the Two-Headed Beast.'

subject: Derro Reading the Ritual Text
fact: A Derro has just begun reading from one of the Trillimac books, potentially activating a ritual, summoning a manifestation, or altering the ambient magic of the cavern. This moment is the precursor to an imminent, unknown event.
source_quote: Just then, one of them picks up a book and starts to read from it.

subject: Identity of Stroud
fact: Stroud is referenced by Grygum as a figure who once inspired him, contrasting with his current boredom with Bahamut. Stroud’s nature, role, and connection to the current events remain unknown, suggesting a deeper backstory yet to be revealed.
source_quote: Bahamut is boring. Stroud was exciting. Bahamut, not so much.

subject: Identity of the Ember Vanguard
fact: The true allegiance of the Ember Vanguard remains ambiguous; its members claim divine authority, but their actions suggest opportunism, and the Derro suspect they serve the Duergar or Mindflayers — a mystery that may unravel later.

subject: purpose of experiments
fact: The experiments are tied to the elevation of the Derro and the triumph of Demogorgon, but their exact nature and mechanics remain unexplained.
source_quote: He shouts - 'We are conducting experiments!'... He screams - 'The only purpose that matters! The elevation of the Derro, the Triumph of Demogorgon, and the destruction of the Duergar!'

subject: Stool's home
fact: Stool wants to return home, but the location of his home is not specified in this session.
source_quote: Jim Jar, Spiderbait, Sarith, Eldeth, and Stool look at me worried

subject: The Great Project of Ulnara
fact: The Great Project of Ulnara involves harvesting body parts for an unknown purpose tied to Demogorgon’s will; its progress is monitored by Derro who fear failure and plead for better jobs, but its ultimate goal remains obscured by madness.

subject: The Prince’s Hunger
fact: The Derro repeatedly reference 'the prince' and his 'hunger,' suggesting a living, consuming entity tied to Demogorgon; this may be a manifestation of the demon lord or a new creation, and its presence is hinted at through the cauldrons and obsidian scales.

subject: True Allegiance of the Ember Guard
fact: The true allegiance of the Ember Guard is unclear. They claim no master, yet operate in the domain of the Duergar and Mindflayers. Their identity may be a fabrication to control Derro, or a genuine but unacknowledged faction with hidden patrons.
source_quote: ‘I don’t believe you guys work for us. I think you work for the Duergar or the Mindflayers!’

subject: Withholding Evidence from Errde
fact: Daz contemplates suppressing the Demogorgon evidence he has found, knowing Errde Blackstaff will fabricate proof if denied. This unresolved tension suggests a future conflict between truth, power, and ideological exploitation.
source_quote: I might not want to give it to her. But I know her type; if she doesn’t get evidence, she’ll invent it.
